cluster_summary: This cluster contains vulnerabilities where user-supplied URLs are passed to browser navigation or external command execution functions without sufficient validation. Missing checks on URL schemes, IP ranges, protocol allowlists, and trust of message sources allow SSRF, command injection, local file access, and unauthorized operations. The cluster includes missing pre-navigation validation, post-interaction re-validation, OS command execution mistakes, insecure trust of messages, and a race condition outlier.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 2 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Validate that the URL starts with a safe scheme (http/https) or does not start with '-', and perform validation after any placeholder substitution..

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Validate that the URL starts with a safe scheme (http/https) or does not start with '-', and perform validation after any placeholder substitution.
sub_patterns.name: Missing URL scheme validation before external command execution
sub_patterns.root_cause: Code passes user-supplied URLs to OS command execution (Runtime.exec, webbrowser.open, shell.openExternal) without checking the scheme or ensuring the string does not start with a dash, allowing arbitrary command injection.
